Asobi Review 1.0 (build 1528) Oct 13, 2026

  • Open a cut in DaVinci Resolve, and read it back. Media ▸ Conformed Cut ▸ Open in DaVinci Resolve… opens the cut in a Resolve project of its own ("Asobi · KNT SPRING v03") with its media linked and each shot's name as a marker, for what Join and Split can't fix. Fix it there, then Read Back from DaVinci Resolve conforms the result as a new cut beside the first: names, joins and Pull Plates choices follow their shots. An offline clip travels as a marked gap and is put back. Asobi asks before leaving a project you have open, and never deletes a project or quits Resolve. Needs Resolve Studio with External scripting set to Local. Settings ▸ Media ▸ Tidy a cut with chooses Automatic, Asobi Only or DaVinci Resolve.
  • Panels stay behind other apps again. In 1.0 (1523) a panel (the Conform window, Pull Plates, the Playlist) stayed floating over every other app when you left Asobi. They now drop behind the app you switch to, in their own order, and a click on one still brings it in front of the others.
  • The manual, corrected. About thirty passages that were wrong, out of date or hard to follow are rewritten, each checked against the app: where licenses are issued and requests arrive in the Review Manager, the color pipeline's three pickers, the sync offset bars, what Import CSV… takes back, the Terminal options of a pull, and more. Chapter 15 gains a section on tidying a cut in DaVinci Resolve.
Earlier updates

1.0 (build 1476) Oct 12, 2026

  • DPX sequences play. 8, 10, 12 and 16-bit DPX files open and play like any other image sequence, read as the color space set for DPX in Settings, Color.
  • A tall floating Playlist with thumbnails could stop the app. Fixed.
  • Small fixes.

1.0 (build 1441) Oct 11, 2026

  • Network is in the Review menu. Review ▸ Network; it was under Window. It is also in the right-click Review menu.
  • A playlist on a network drive no longer slows the window. Whether each clip's file is there is checked in the background.
  • Locate Media… reads a folder in the background. A line above the toolbar says how far it has got.

Asobi Review 1.0 (build 1523) Oct 13, 2026

  • The manual is easier to scan. Long blocks of text are broken into short paragraphs under sub-headings, in the app and in the PDF: chapter 15 (Conform and plate pulls) went from 6 sub-headings to 75, and the other long chapters the same way. More space between paragraphs and list items, numbered steps shown as steps, and a new section on Export Cut. No procedure changed.
  • Export Cut. Media ▸ Conformed Cut ▸ Export Cut… writes the cut as it now stands into a folder: an OTIO of every track, a CMX3600 EDL for each track, and a marker list. Every event is where the cut has it, with its speed; each shot carries its name as a marker (the names Pull Plates gives, once its window has been opened on the cut), and a joined shot has one marker over all its events. Conformed again in Asobi, the exported cut comes back with the same shots, names and joins. DaVinci Resolve keeps the events, speeds and shot markers of the OTIO. A reposition is not written into the cut, and a speed that changes through a clip is written as its average.
  • A click on a panel brings that panel in front of the others. Panels now stay on one level among themselves, so any of them can be brought forward by clicking it, and they keep their order when you switch to another app and back.
  • Markers from DaVinci Resolve, checked against Resolve's own export. Timeline markers and clip markers in an OTIO from Resolve name and join shots as described for 1517. A marker's Notes are now read as well, so a shot's ID typed in the Notes of a marker still called "Marker 3" names the shot. Send the cut from Resolve as OTIO: its EDL and XML exports leave markers out.

Asobi Review 1.0 (build 1517) Oct 13, 2026

  • A pull that Asobi didn't see end is offered back. If Asobi quit, crashed or the Mac shut down while plates were being written, the next launch shows a line at the top of the window: "3 plates of KNT SPRING v03 were not finished." Resume opens the cut as it was when the pull began, saved or not, and writes what is left in the same version; a part-written plate is written again from its first frame. If the shots folder or a source isn't mounted it says which drive and starts nothing. Not Now leaves them, and the cut's Pull Plates window still offers what is left. A pull you stopped yourself is never offered back.
  • The editor's markers name and join shots. A conform now reads the markers in the cut: locators in an EDL, and markers on a clip, a track or the timeline in an OTIO. A marker whose text is a shot's ID (KNT_SPR_045) names the shot in Pull Plates, after a name you typed and before Asobi's own numbering, which steps around it. A marker that runs over several events of one take, or one name on events that butt, joins them into one shot; Split undoes it. Other markers are the editor's comments, shown with the clip in the Conform window. The cut's summary says how many shots the markers named and joined, and the Conform report lists every marker. Markers in AAF and XML cuts are not read yet.
  • Find Originals finds the EXR frames. In Media ▸ Clip Locations…, Find Originals now sees frames kept in a folder named for the version alone (renders/comp/v001/), which it used to pass over for a movie. A new Prefer pop-up beside the button says which is a clip's original where its version has both: Image Sequences (the default) or Movies. A clip that only has the other kind gets that, and the line under the button says how many did.
